name: input.mouse.release
description: Release a mouse button if held by anything (this connection or another). Idempotent — returns `OK 0` whether or not the button was held. Use to lift a button held by `input.mouse.press`, or as a cross-connection fail-safe to recover from a stuck state. Per issue #67.

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`. Idempotent: no error if the button wasn't held. The agent removes the button from any connection's held-input set (cross-connection cleanup permitted; see lifecycle §2.8).

x-implementations.name: send_input
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SendInput` with INPUT_MOUSE + the appropriate `MOUSEEVENTF_*UP` flag. No matching down event. Always issued — the OS no-ops gracefully when the button wasn't actually down.

x-implementations.name: mouse_event
x-implementations.description: Win32 `mouse_event` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where SendInput is unavailable.

windows-modern.description: SendInput with MOUSEEVENTF_*UP. Agent removes the button from the per-connection held-input set (and any other connection's set that holds it — cross-connection release is the documented fail-safe). Idempotent — no `not_held` error since the verb's purpose is cleanup. UIPI does not apply on the up event in practice (the kernel sends the up event regardless of where the button was pressed).

windows-classic.description: SendInput on NT 5+; mouse_event on NT 4 / 9x. Same idempotent cross-connection-release semantics as modern.
